calls.reason: Weidinger et al. (Dec 2021) already anticipated self-harm assistance, harmful misinformation, unsafe reliance, privacy leakage and addictive uses, which are most of the complaint's categories. No evidence shows any category was unforeseeable.

AP reporting confirms federal legislation stalled, but IAPP counts 11 states with preventive chatbot laws, and Florida law allows injunctions against likely violations. How well those alternatives work is unestablished.

Anthropic and CRS records show only Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were pulled, with other models unaffected, so 'entire industry' is hyperbole. But the main point, that arbitrary government stops industries thriving, is an untested maxim.

Anthropic's 2025 filings show repeated calls for chip export controls, and Sacks mentioned its lobbying. But Sacks blamed the directive on Anthropic refusing to fix the jailbreak, and no record shows how much the advocacy or any overselling mattered.

Anthropic's account confirms Amazon's bypass report came before the directive. Peer-reviewed 2024–25 research shows broad jailbreak susceptibility across major models, and every model Anthropic tested reproduced the demonstration. 'Panicked' is Marcus's hedged opinion.

Moussouris, who read the report, describes plain 'fix this code' requests, not a novel bypass. Anthropic's tests found every model tested produced the same exploit demonstration, so the behaviour was neither new nor specific to Fable or Mythos.
